title: Few blues in his own band repertoire
summary: Carter did few blues, naming D Blues and Big Ben Blues.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: But I was -- I'm sort of getting at sort of a larger perspective of maybe a larger body of work here, and I don't know if these observations -- if you agree with these or not, but in looking at, say, your work from the 1930's as a general enough statement right there, that in the things that you would offer under your own name -- Benny Carter and his orchestra -- and there are a couple of generalizations that might be made about just the material you presented under your own name.
There's very little blues, for example. Is that a reasonable generalization? Or relative to what other people might have been doing at that time?
No, I guess I just didn't think along those terms, too much. You know what I mean? What did I do in the way of blues -- I did some blues. Not too many, though, did I?
"D Blues" -- that was with the Chocolate Dandies. "Big Ben Blues" in England. What else did I do in blues? "Blues in My Heart" which was really not the blues.
I can't recall anything else, can you? : Not off hand. I'm really groping around.
Yeah. So am I! No ... I don't know.
